ms until the server bids 0 for the seat, from serverTime (relative: never compare with a client clock)

signUp.notes: Two per-socket budgets. The wrapper limit rateLimiter.signUp (20 / 5 min) counts every attempt and over it replies error {type:'rateLimit'}. Refusals by the new-name rules, the profanity filter and the taken check spend only that; an attempt past them (bcrypt hash + insert) also spends rateLimiter.signUpAccount (3 / 5 min), checked in-handler, and over it gets signUpResponse {success:false, message}. The same attempt also spends budgets a reconnect does not reset (rateLimiter.buckets, all checked before any is spent, and before signUpAccount): signUpIp per client IP, an IPv6 address by its /64 (5 at once, then 5 an hour; skipped when the IP is unknown), signUpNet48 per IPv6 /48 (10 at once, then 10 an hour) and signUpGlobal for the whole server (20 at once, then 60 an hour); over any of them it gets signUpResponse {success:false, message} too.

restoreSession.notes: Wrapper limit 10 / min per socket (every reconnect is a new socket, so it never meets a flaky network); over it serverError {code:'rateLimit'}, never a restoreSessionResponse failure, which makes iOS forget its saved token.

clientHello.notes: Sent on every connect by clients that read avatarUrl / avatarUrls ($defs.clientCap). No reply. Absent = legacy shape (iOS 1.1.0, cached old web bundles); iOS sends it from 1.2.0 (SocketService, on every connect before restoreSession). Unknown caps are ignored; the last hello wins (one without avatarUrl downgrades the socket). Over the rate limit it is dropped silently. Logged with the client version (telemetry for V1_REMOVALS). Caps the server acts on: avatarUrl, casualSpectators, playAgain, assist, tutorial (2026-11-19: the client renders the tutorial's tips and assistState, and only such a socket gets the tutorial's auto-start; $defs.clientCapTutorial), shoulderView (2026-11-21: the over-the-shoulder view, watchHand and every shoulder key; without it none is sent, and a hello that drops it ends the socket's watch; $defs.clientCapShoulderView), and tournamentVoice (2026-11-24: the client starts voice on its tournament lobby screen and at a tournament table, so it is a peer of the tournament's voice room and announced at its table's seating; without it a socket is never listed in the tournament room; $defs.clientCapTournamentVoice), and tournamentPairings (2026-11-25: the client shows the tournament events' pairings and, at a tournament table, startDraw.teams / snapshot draw.teams as a draw for first deal; a tournament table draws honestly, each player the card they picked, only when every human there and every spectator present at its startDraw has it, else the draw is staged as before; $defs.clientCapTournamentPairings).

changePassword.notes: New (2026-11-15). The signed-in socket's own account only. Answered by changePasswordResponse {success, message}. next must be 8-100 characters and differ from current (checked in the handler, so Joi stays 1-100 and a short one gets the rule message); the current-password check counts in the failed-sign-in throttle like deleteAccount's. On success every saved session but this device's is revoked, every other live socket of the account gets forceLogout, and open reset links are cancelled. Rate limit 5 / 5 min per socket. Web: profile page, Change password. iOS: Account sheet, Change Password, from the next build after 1.2.1 build 9 (sentBy says what shipped clients send).

examples.message: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'x')

clientError.notes: Additive 2026-11-15: a short technical report of a client-side error (server/socket/clientErrorHandlers.js). Never answered, never serverError: a payload Joi refuses, a report over a limit and every report while CLIENT_ERRORS=off are dropped silently. Limits: 5 a minute and 50 a day per socket, plus per-IP and server-wide buckets (rateLimiter.buckets clientErrorIp / clientErrorGlobal). Logged at warn with the signed-in username and every text field scrubbed (URL queries and fragments, emails, ids, long digit runs, IPs, quoted text), never chat. Web sends it (client/src/telemetry/clientErrors.js: uncaught errors, unhandled rejections, SeqGate gaps, TableDirector failures, illegal screen transitions; once per kind per session, only while connected, a few buffered before). iOS sends it from the build after 1.2.1 build 9 (ErrorReporter.swift: undecodable table events and snapshots, the unreadable table, seq gaps, unexpected socket errors, an uncaught exception saved and sent on the next launch); 1.2.0 through 1.2.1 build 9 never send it.

deleteAccount.notes: The password check also counts in the failed-sign-in throttle (server/socket/signInThrottle.js: per username / IP across sockets); throttled, it answers deleteAccountResponse {success:false, message} before any hash.

createLobby.notes: mode (additive 2026-11-24; the web sends it, no iOS build): gyb opens a Get Your Bid lobby (3 seats, no teams; server/game/gameMode.js), only from a socket that sent the clientHello cap getYourBid (else serverError); absent or classic is the base game.

joinLobby.notes: Joi since V1_REMOVALS #18 (2026-11-11): lobby ids are uuids (web MainRoom / ClientSession re-entry and iOS 1.1.0 LobbyEmitter.joinLobby send {lobbyId}).

addBot.notes: The handler ignores the payload; iOS sends {personality}.

setSpectatorsCanTalk.notes: New (2026-11-16, family lobbies); IGNORED since 2026-11-18 (owner: "we don't need the spectator voice host toggle, just having it default on is good"): spectators always may talk, so nothing changes it. Sent by iOS 1.2.2 (build 12) to 1.2.3 (build 15) (the lobby host's Toggle, GameLobbyView, and the in-game switch in the voice panel while voiceSettings.canChange, VoicePanelSheet; LobbyEmitter.setSpectatorsCanTalk) and by web bundles cached from before that day; neither the web nor later iOS builds have the switch. Accepted from anyone and answered with the unchanged settings, never an error (that echo repeats the value the client already holds, which those builds do not take as the answer: an old lobby Toggle switched off shows Off, disabled, until its own 5 s echo timeout puts it back On; sending false first would only flash it): in a lobby a playerReadyUpdate (the plain variant, settings {spectatorsCanTalk: true}) to the sender only (it still counts as acting in the lobby: play again settles it); in a casual game the sender's voiceSettings (spectatorsCanTalk true, canChange false); anywhere else nothing (debug log). Wrapper limit 4 / 30 s per socket (an over-limit send still gets serverError rateLimit).

releaseLobbyHold.notes: New (2026-11-16, play again). Web sends it (GameLobby: "Don't wait" on a row marked members[].returning or an expected name, shown to the host, or to anyone present while the host is away); iOS from 1.2.2 (build 12): "Don't wait for <name>" on a returning row or an expected name of the lobby (GameLobbyView; LobbyEmitter.releaseLobbyHold), shown to the host, or to anyone present while the host is held. "Don't wait for <name>" in a lobby reopened after a game (server/socket/playAgain.js): releases that user's hold (a row marked members[].returning) or reservation (expected) at once, as its expiry would: a leave that keeps everyone's ready flags. The lobby host only; while the host is away (held), any present member. Anyone else, a socket in no lobby, or a name with nothing held: serverError {code: 'rejected'}. Wrapper limit 10 / 30 s per socket.

lobbyReturnSeen.notes: New (2026-11-16, play again; additive). Sent when the person leaves the last game's results for the lobby lobbyReturn kept behind them, i.e. whenever the client puts that lobby on screen. iOS from 1.2.2 (build 12): LobbyReturn.enter, from GameEndView's Return to Lobby, its own entry when that game's gameEnd never applied within 5 s, and a lobbyReturn that arrived off the table (main room, lobby screen). Web (main.js returnToReopenedLobby -> ClientSession.returnToReopenedLobby, then its joinLobby): the score modal's Return to Lobby landing in that lobby, its only entry (its seq gate applies a held gameEnd within 5 s, GAP_TIMEOUT_MS, so the modal always comes; a lobbyReturn in the main room leaves that lobby instead; one that started its next game meanwhile lands in the main room, already out of it). The results stay up until that tap (owner 2026-11-16), so without it the server cannot tell the score screen from the lobby screen: the socket stays in lobby.afterGame.unsettled until it acts in the lobby. Settles it (server/socket/playAgain.js lobbyReturnSeen -> settle): a later drop is the ordinary 30 s reload grace (no "Not back yet" hold), another socket of the same user no longer takes the seat on its joinMainRoom (autoClaimTarget), and at the next start it is an extra like any member (an unsettled one gets leftLobby instead of spectatorJoined: GameManager.startGameFromLobby onResults, playAgain.leftOnResults). No reply; when it settled the socket, the lobby's other capable members get a playerReadyUpdate (neither) whose members no longer mark its row onResults ("Still on the results", additive 2026-11-16: playAgain.announceSettled); a socket in no lobby, or already settled, changes nothing. Wrapper limit 10 / 30 s per socket.

removeBot.notes: Joi since V1_REMOVALS #18 (2026-11-11): a payload is required and only a bot id (bot:...) passes; GameManager.removeBotFromLobby also refuses a human member. Web (GameLobby) and iOS 1.1.0 (LobbyEmitter.removeBot) send {botSocketId}; only the gated 1.0.0 sent no payload.

playerBid.notes: Web sends a string; iOS an Int for numeric bids and a string for bores. 13 / '13' passes Joi (both clients offer 0...hand size) and is refused by the handler (actionRejected invalid_bid) unless the hand has 13 cards.

chatMessage.notes: /lazy, /active and /leave are seat commands. /help (2026-11-18) and the exact line ?help (any case, surrounding spaces ignored: the only way shipped iOS builds can ask, since they refuse unknown / commands on the device) ask for a suggestion (server/socket/assistHandlers.js): never broadcast or stored as chat; the reply is private (s2c assistHint with the clientHello cap assist, else private gameLogEntry lines), and a counted use posts the room line "<name> used /help.". "?help me" is ordinary chat.

watchHand.notes: New (2026-11-21, the over-the-shoulder view). Web sends it from 2026-11-21 (client/src/state/shoulder.js: the default watch after each full state, an avatar click, Table view; iOS from the build after 1.2.3 (30): State/Table/Shoulder.swift, the same rules, ActionCoordinator sends it). A pure spectator with the clientHello cap shoulderView watches seat `position` (1-4) read-only, or stops (null). Accepted: stateSnapshot {snapshot, reason: 'watchHand', requestId?} (viewer.shoulder while watching), then the table's coalesced spectatorsUpdated; every later deal's spectator gameStart carries shoulder, and the watched seat's hints come as assistHint {watched}. Refused: watchHandRefused {gameId, position, reason, message, ownPosition?}. From a socket without the cap it is dropped silently (no reply). The watch is never saved and goes with the socket's spectator entry: re-send it after a spectatorJoined full state without viewer.shoulder (a reconnect on a new socket, spectating another game and back, a deploy-survival adoption); re-spectating the same game from the same socket keeps it, and re-sending watchHand is idempotent. A stop (null) is always done (no reply while the table is suspended or frozen); after an unavailable refusal keep the selection and re-send after "Game resumed." or the next full state. docs/claude/spectators.md "Over-the-shoulder view".

requestSnapshot.notes: New in snapshot v2. Answered by stateSnapshot to this socket only. customPics is accepted and ignored since V1_REMOVALS #19 C (no snapshot carries an inline picture; web and iOS 1.2.0 send customPics:false). Web always sends {requestId, customPics:false, log:false}: "ping-*" its liveness ping after the tab was hidden > 5 s (item 15; a reconnect only when no reply arrives), "gap-*" on a seq gap (debounced: one in flight), "ack-*" when its bid/play got no answer for 5 s (item 16); every reply with a snapshot of its table is applied and rendered.

getProfile.notes: iOS from 1.2.2 (build 10): the own profile in the Account sheet; it always sends {scope} (human included), so every success carries the echo. Throttled in-handler (rateLimiter key getProfile, 20 / 10 s per socket); over the limit serverError {code:'rateLimit', handler:'getProfile'}, as the wrappers answer. Optional {scope: human | bots | all} (additive 2026-11-13): human = games with no bot or resign-bot seat at the end (users.stats, today's reply), bots = games with one (users.botStats, gameRecords withBots), all = both summed field by field. Missing, non-object or unknown = human, never refused. The reply echoes `scope` only when the request carried the key. iOS sends no payload (human).

updateProfilePic.notes: iOS from 1.2.2 (build 10): Account sheet, Choose Avatar. Answered by profilePicUpdateResponse.

uploadProfilePic.notes: iOS from 1.2.2 (build 10): Account sheet, Upload Photo (a 200 px PNG data URL, cropped to a circle with 16% padding like the web's). Pipeline on (docs/avatars.md): decoded and re-encoded server-side; stored as a WebP data URL <= 256 px; undecodable or unsafe images are refused with the usual {success:false, message}.

getLeaderboard.notes: Throttled in-handler (rateLimiter key getLeaderboard, one budget for every scope); over the limit replies leaderboardResponse with that scope's cached (possibly stale) result, else its fill in flight, else the existing {success:false, message} reply; never error. Served from a 60 s cache per scope, every scope invalidated on stats/picture/account changes. Optional {scope: human | bots | all} (additive 2026-11-13): human = games with no bot or resign-bot seat at the end (users.stats, today's reply), bots = games with one (users.botStats, gameRecords withBots), all = both summed field by field. Missing, non-object or unknown = human, never refused. The reply echoes `scope` only when the request carried the key. iOS sends no payload (human).

getRecords.notes: Throttled in-handler (rateLimiter key getRecords, one budget for every scope); over the limit replies recordsResponse with that scope's cached (possibly stale) result, else its fill in flight, else the existing {success:false, message} reply; never error. Served from a 60 s cache per scope (per month), every scope invalidated when a game is recorded or an account deleted. Optional {scope: human | bots | all} (additive 2026-11-13): human = games with no bot or resign-bot seat at the end (users.stats, today's reply), bots = games with one (users.botStats, gameRecords withBots), all = both summed field by field. Missing, non-object or unknown = human, never refused. The reply echoes `scope` only when the request carried the key. iOS sends no payload (human).

searchPlayers.notes: Joi since V1_REMOVALS #18 (2026-11-11). A blank query answers {success:false} and a trimmed query longer than 50 (the username max) an empty list, in the handler.

getPlayerProfile.notes: iOS from 1.2.2 (build 10): the player profile sheet (chat long-press View Profile, a seat avatar tap, the online list), always with {scope}; a bot name is asked too and answers Player not found. Joi since V1_REMOVALS #18 (2026-11-11). Web asks from search rows, seat avatars and opponent plates (dataset.username, a bot name included). Optional {scope: human | bots | all} (additive 2026-11-13): human = games with no bot or resign-bot seat at the end (users.stats, today's reply), bots = games with one (users.botStats, gameRecords withBots), all = both summed field by field. Missing, non-object or unknown = human, never refused. The reply echoes `scope` only when the request carried the key. iOS sends no payload (human). Joi accepts any scope value (lenient: the handler normalizes a non-string, null or unknown scope to human, echoed).

setTournamentRounds.notes: New (2026-11-25): the host picks the number of rounds, 1 to 5 (default 4), in the tournament lobby before Begin. Accepted: tournamentSettingsUpdated {totalRounds, by} and an unstored system tournamentMessage "<host> set the tournament to 3 rounds." to the room, then lobbiesUpdated; ready flags are kept; the same count again sends nothing. Refused with serverError: 'Not in a tournament', 'Only the host can change the number of rounds', 'Rounds can only change before the tournament begins'. Web sends it from the lobby's Rounds picker (ui/screens/TournamentLobby.js); iOS from build 41.

cutForABuckDraw.notes: New (2026-11-25, Cut for a buck; server/socket/cutForABuck.js draw): a draw for the open round (the round of the last cutForABuckRound), the slot clicked in the face-down fan, or null for a random one. Answered by the room's cutForABuckDrew. Anything out of turn (no tournament, not phase cut, no open round, a stale round, not a player still in, a repeat, a spectator) is dropped silently (no serverError); a malformed payload gets the wrapper's serverError {code: 'validation'}. Rate limit 10 / 10 s. Sent by the web from the Cut for a buck PR and iOS from build 41 (sentBy says what shipped clients send).

voiceOffer.notes: Forwarded only to a connected socket id (never a room) of a signed-in peer in the sender's lobby or game (entrant / seat owner; not a pure spectator), when neither user blocked the other, within the per-socket limit rateLimiter.voiceOffer (30 / 10 s), and when the payload passes validators.schemas.voiceOffer (joiInHandler, V1_REMOVALS #18), all checked in-handler; anything else is dropped silently (no reply, never error). iOS 1.1.0 sends username "" when it has none; the server forwards its own name.

voiceAnswer.notes: Forwarded only to a connected socket id (never a room) of a signed-in peer in the sender's lobby or game (entrant / seat owner; not a pure spectator), when neither user blocked the other, within the per-socket limit rateLimiter.voiceAnswer (30 / 10 s), and when the payload passes validators.schemas.voiceAnswer (joiInHandler, V1_REMOVALS #18), all checked in-handler; anything else is dropped silently (no reply, never error).

voiceIceCandidate.notes: Forwarded only to a connected socket id (never a room) of a signed-in peer in the sender's lobby or game (entrant / seat owner; not a pure spectator), when neither user blocked the other, within the per-socket limit rateLimiter.voiceIceCandidate (300 / 10 s), and when the payload passes validators.schemas.voiceIceCandidate (joiInHandler, V1_REMOVALS #18), all checked in-handler; anything else is dropped silently (no reply, never error). Web sends RTCIceCandidate.toJSON() (usernameFragment, nulls), iOS 1.1.0 {candidate, sdpMLineIndex, sdpMid} ("" for a nil sdpMid).

getVoiceIceServers.notes: Answered by voiceIceServers to this socket only (requestId echoed). Web asks before its first peer connection of a voice session and again before the credentials expire. TURN credentials (Cloudflare Realtime, minted server-side, cached per user) only for a signed-in socket that is a voice peer now (in a lobby, or an entrant / seat owner of a game); everyone else, and every failure (env unset, Cloudflare timeout or error), gets the public STUN servers. iOS 1.1.0 does not send it (it hard-codes STUN); iOS 1.2.0 asks on every voice start and before its restart (Voice/IceServerStore.swift; V1_REMOVALS "iOS TURN").

adminRequest.notes: The admin panel (server/socket/adminHandlers.js). Answered by adminResponse to this socket only (requestId and action echoed). Authorized on EVERY request against the database (signed in, the account's current socket, its session still live, not a merged tombstone, isAdmin true); anyone else gets {ok:false, error:'forbidden'} for every action and target, before args are read, so a non-admin learns nothing. args are validated per action after that (adminHandlers ACTION_SCHEMAS; invalid -> {ok:false, error:'invalid'}). Each request writes one adminAudit entry (listAudit excepted). Wrapper limit 60/min (serverError {code:'rateLimit', handler:'adminRequest'}, never an adminResponse). Sent by the web panel and, from iOS 1.2.2 build 10, by the iOS admin panel (Networking/AdminApi.swift: the same requestId matching, 15 s timeout and 3 s rate-limit fail-fast; only on a connected socket whose sign-in or restore was answered, so a forbidden answer always means the access is gone). iOS 1.2.0 / 1.2.1 never send it. No platform check on the server: every socket is authorized the same way.

signInResponse.notes: isAdmin (additive, 2026-11-11; present only when true): the web menu shows its Admin entry. Display only: the server re-checks the database on every adminRequest. iOS up to 1.2.1 reads the reply as a dictionary and ignores the key; from 1.2.2 build 10 it shows the Account sheet's Admin entry (AuthState.isAdmin). passwordReset {by: link | admin, at: ISO time} (additive 2026-11-15, success only): the password was reset since the player last signed in, by a one-time reset link or by an admin (scripts/set-password.js); sent once (the reply's session write clears it). Web shows one info line ("Your password was reset with a reset link on <date>. If that wasn't you, tell an admin."); iOS from the next build after 1.2.1 build 9; iOS 1.2.0 ignores it.

updateRequired.notes: New (2026-11-25, private, unsequenced): only an upgrade-gated iOS socket (User-Agent build below the gate: MIN_IOS_BUILD, raised and never lowered by the env BAB_MIN_IOS_BUILD) gets it, with the gate's main push (2 s after connect, beside mainRoomJoined) and then once a minute (every 10th REPEAT_MS repeat), so the timed pushes stay within the gate's 20 emits per minute. message is the gate's update text, url the App Store page. The builds gated today (1.0.0, 1.1.0) and builds 39 / 40 ignore it (no handler); iOS from build 41 shows it as a full-screen update screen with an App Store button and keeps the saved session, so the next gate past 41 is seen on every screen.

restoreSessionResponse.notes: isAdmin: as on signInResponse (display only, present only when true; iOS up to 1.2.1 ignores it, 1.2.2 shows its Admin entry). passwordReset {by: link | admin, at: ISO time} (additive 2026-11-15, success only): the password was reset since the player last signed in, by a one-time reset link or by an admin (scripts/set-password.js); sent once (the reply's session write clears it). Web shows one info line ("Your password was reset with a reset link on <date>. If that wasn't you, tell an admin."); iOS from the next build after 1.2.1 build 9; iOS 1.2.0 ignores it. retryable: true (additive 2026-11-15, failure only) when the failure is passing and the saved token may still be good: a database error (also the session re-check's failed read) or a name an admin merge / rename / delete holds for a moment ("This account is being updated..."). Web keeps the saved token, shows Reconnecting... and sends restoreSession again with backoff (1 s doubling to 30 s, within the 10 / min limit); iOS the same from the next build after 1.2.1 build 9. iOS 1.2.0 and 1.2.1 up to build 9 ignore the key and forget the token on any failure (sign-in screen), as before. Every other failure (no such user, a deleted name, a bad or revoked token) has no retryable and both clients forget the token.

sessionSuperseded.notes: New (2026-11-11). One live connection per user: a newer socket of the SAME saved session (another web tab adopting it, or a reload whose old socket the server still holds) took over; this socket is parked. Sent once when it happens and again (refused: the event name, at most once a second, with the reason it was last told) for every event the parked socket sends other than signIn / signUp / restoreSession / clientHello, which are dropped, never answered with error. Web: a full-screen notice, "Use here" reconnects and restores, which parks the other tab. reason 'otherClosed' (additive, 2026-11-11): the user's LIVE socket disconnected and, 2 s later (OTHER_CLOSED_DELAY_MS: a reload of that tab re-takes the session first and nothing is sent), no socket holds the session; only that user's parked sockets are told, and nothing is taken back by itself (web: "The other BAB Online tab was closed. Use here to continue."). A socket that takes the session after that sends 'newerConnection' again to the parked sockets told 'otherClosed' (reparkClosedNotices). Limitation: a parked socket never restores, so one that reconnected (a deploy, a network blip) is anonymous to the server and told nothing more; the web notice then says only that the other tab may still be open. Web Sign Out revokes no token: a parked web tab signs itself out when the device's saved session is gone (the storage event, 'otherClosed', Use here). iOS 1.1.0 has no handler (unknown events are ignored) and never shares a token between live sockets, so it never has a parked socket; a different session gets forceLogout as before.

deleteAccountResponse.notes: Refused (success false, the message says why) while the player is in a live game (its draw included, a /leave'd seat until the game ends) or a tournament that is not complete (2026-11-15). On success the name is held for 30 days (a deleted-name tombstone: sign-up says it is taken; an admin can free it in the panel).

changePasswordResponse.notes: New (2026-11-15): the reply to changePassword. success true: the password changed, every other device was signed out (forceLogout to its live sockets, its saved session revoked); this device stays signed in. success false: message says why (the 8-100 rule, the same password, a wrong current password (counted in the failed-sign-in throttle), throttled, busy, a database error). Web: the profile page's Change password form; iOS from the next build after 1.2.1 build 9 (Account sheet). Shipped iOS builds never send changePassword, so never get it.

activeGameFound.notes: Never emitted (signInResponse.activeGameId replaced it). CAUTION: the only event that makes the shipped iOS app emit rejoinGame by itself (AuthSocketHandler.handleActiveGameFound); see V1_REMOVALS.md.

blockListUpdated.notes: Also sent unasked (success, with silent: true) to a player whose saved block list an admin RENAME re-pointed (accountDelete.refreshBlockLists), so the renamed player's chat stays hidden; both clients replace their list. Web shows its "Block list updated" info toast only without silent. The App Store iOS build (1.1.0, f05d264) ignores silent and shows its "Block list updated." alert (SafetySocketHandler / .safetyAlerts) wherever the player is: accepted for renames, which are rare and owner-run; so do 1.2.0 through 1.2.1 build 9. iOS reads silent from 1.2.2 (build 10; SafetySocketHandler.applyBlockListUpdated: list replaced, no alert). An admin DELETE sends nothing (the dead name stays in the client list, harmless, until the next sign-in; only the voice list is refreshed), and a player's own Delete account leaves other players' lists alone.

mainRoomJoined.notes: recentMessages (a copy of messages) is sent only by upgradeGate.sendMainRoom, to the gated iOS 1.0.0, which reads it first. The main-room handlers dropped it (V1_REMOVALS #13, 2026-11-11): web reads messages and iOS 1.1.0 recentMessages ?? messages (LobbySocketHandler, f05d264). inProgressGames is the joiner's own list (GameManager.getInProgressGames(username)): the ambient demo game only for the AMBIENT_CHAT_USERS accounts (owner, 2026-11-14), like the bot lines in messages.

mainRoomMessage.notes: mainRoom: a human line (and an ambient bot line when AMBIENT_CHAT_USERS=*); socket: an ambient bot line to each main-room socket of an AMBIENT_CHAT_USERS account (default test1; server/utils/ambientChatUsers.js).

mainRoomPlayerJoined.notes: A refresh of the online count and list (both clients: no chat line). Sent (1) on joinMainRoom, socket.to(mainRoom): everyone in the main room but the joiner; (2) since 2026-11-20, io.to(mainRoom) when a sign-in, sign-up, restoreSession or token rejoin brings a name online that was not (a player reconnecting straight into a game or tournament never sends joinMainRoom); a second socket of a user already online sends none. A client that then joins the main room causes (1) too: one more identical refresh.

mainRoomPlayerLeft.notes: New: a name went offline (the online list shrank): its last socket disconnected (queueHandlers.handleDisconnect, also an account switch on the socket) or it was signed out (authHandlers.signOutSocket: sign out everywhere, a password reset, an admin action). Counterpart of mainRoomPlayerJoined. Both clients replace the online count and list from it, as for mainRoomPlayerJoined: the web from 2026-11-20, iOS from the build after 1.2.3 (24) (LobbySocketHandler.applyOnlineList); iOS 1.2.3 (24) and older ignore it and keep a stale list until the next join.

reserved.why: iOS reads lobbyName ?? name

Sent to the game room on every change (join, leave, disconnect, spectating another game, a round start, a reclaim), coalesced to one emit per game per 250 ms, skipped when unchanged, never after end/abort. UNSEQUENCED (no seq, no bump; GameState.emitUnsequenced): an absolute display state, and the App Store build (f05d264) registers no handler for it, so a sequenced form would open a gap in its seq gate on every change. The snapshot's `watching` carries the same {spectators, count}. iOS 1.1.0 reads nothing; iOS 1.2.0 routes it around its seq gate (ServerEvent.spectators) and shows the badge (V1_REMOVALS "iOS spectator badge").

inMs.description: ms from emission until the server bids 0 for the seat (relative: measure from receipt with a monotonic clock, never compare with a wall clock)

durationMs.description: the clock's full length (30000 by default), the countdown's scale

bidClock.notes: The bid clock (owner 2026-11-18, every game; contract/README.md "Bid clock"): a human-controlled seat that has not bid 10 s (SeatState.BID_CLOCK_DELAY_MS) after its bid turn opened gets a 30 s clock (BID_CLOCK_MS, the length of bidclock.m4a, the tune the table plays); when it runs out the server bids '0' for the seat through the normal bid path, after the room log line "<name> ran out of time.". `running` carries the time left from emission (inMs) and the full length (durationMs): clients END-align the tune with the deadline and show the bidder a countdown with a small safety margin. `stopped` reasons: bid (the seat bid), timeout (the server is bidding 0 right after: let the tune's end cue ring), turn (the turn moved some other way, e.g. a new deal), controller (a bot took the seat: /lazy, AFK, resign, /leave). No stopped on gameEnd / abortGame (terminal games emit nothing): clients clear the clock on those and on every bidReceived / updateTurn / doneBidding / gameStart / destroyHands / snapshot without bidClock. A `running` is never sent before the 10 s pre-wait except on a same-turn resume (/active, reclaimSeat), which a client-side seq-gap replay of older events cannot clear. Bots never get one. UNSEQUENCED (no seq, no bump; GameState.emitUnsequenced), like spectatorsUpdated: the payload is absolute and every shipped iOS build (<= 1.2.3 (14)) registers no handler for it, so a sequenced form would open a gap in their seq gate on every clock start and stop; no clientHello cap (unknown unsequenced events are invisible to old clients). Timeouts in a row (BID_TIMEOUT_AFK_STRIKES, default 2): when a timeout is a connected seat's Nth in a row (casual tables, and tournament tables with no other owner present; not solo / AFK-exempt games, not with AFK_TIMEOUT_MS=0), a bot takes the seat in the same run: playerLazyMode and its "was idle" log line come after that bidReceived '0' and before the updateTurn / doneBidding / redeal it triggers. Shipped builds see only the log line and the ordinary bidReceived '0'; the next iOS build after 1.2.3 (14) registers it and routes it around its seq gate (ServerEvent.bidClock, decoded with seq nil: the tune, the bidder's countdown, the timeout toast). Snapshot v2 carries the running clock as the optional `bidClock`.

watchHandRefused.notes: New (2026-11-21, the over-the-shoulder view; private, unsequenced): c2s watchHand refused (read by the web from 2026-11-21: client/src/state/shoulder.js onRefused; iOS from the build after 1.2.3 (30): TableReducer.watchRefused, State/Table/Shoulder.swift); nothing changed (a hand already watched stays watched). Only ever sent to a socket with the clientHello cap shoulderView: a watchHand from a socket without it is dropped silently (no reply at all). Reasons, checked in this order: not_spectating (not a pure spectator of that game: unknown or other game, a seat owner, a lazy watcher, an entrant), unavailable (the table is suspended by the LIVE_PERSIST self-fence, frozen by a handoff, or over: try again after the resume), tournament (never at tournament tables, known by the game itself, so also after its tournament was cancelled or deleted while the table lives), not_dealt (before the first gameStart: CREATED, the draw, the teams), own_seat (the socket's user owns a seat at this table, gone included: it may watch only that seat, ownPosition). Stopping (position null) is refused only for not_spectating: a stop exposes nothing, so it is always done, and on a suspended, frozen or ended table it gets no reply at all (no snapshot leaves such a table). Clients: after unavailable keep the selected seat (the server keeps a watch across a suspension, it just serves nothing meanwhile) and send watchHand again after the room's 'Game resumed.' line or the next full state. message is short English a client may show. A malformed payload (position not 1-4 or null, a bad gameId) is the wrapper's serverError {code: 'validation'} instead, and the rate limit's serverError {code: 'rateLimit'}. docs/claude/spectators.md "Over-the-shoulder view".

seatLeft.notes: New (2026-11-19, additive): a seat's owner left the game for good (/leave from the seat or from watching a lazy / resigned seat: presence gone, absorbing; the bot keeps the seat). Before it the room heard a /leave from a human seat only as playerLazyMode (an already-lazy owner's not at all), the same as a /lazy owner still watching, and only a snapshot (seats[].presence gone) told them apart. Read by the web (state: GameState.applySeatLeft) and by iOS 1.2.3 (18), the first upload of the build 17 source (TestFlight's 1.2.3 (17) is build 16's code, renumbered by Organizer; GameSocketHandler, ServerEvent.seatLeft decoded with seq nil around its seq gate; TableReducer.seatLeft sets the seat's presence gone): voice runs only while another human is present (owner 2026-11-19, docs/claude/voice.md "No voice alone"; a gone owner no longer counts). UNSEQUENCED (no seq, no bump; GameState.emitUnsequenced): the fact is absorbing and a later snapshot shows it, and every shipped iOS build (<= 17: TestFlight's 1.2.3 (17) is build 16's code, renumbered by Organizer) registers no handler for it, so a sequenced form would open a gap in their seq gate; no clientHello cap (unknown unsequenced events are invisible to old clients). Never sent from a terminal game; when the /leave ends the game (no owner left who could return) abortGame follows it in the same tick. Sent after the leaver's socket left the room, so the leaver never gets it.

New (2026-11-18, /help plan H2c; private, unsequenced. Web reads it from 2026-11-19 (H3: the clientHello cap assist, client/src/ui/components/AssistCard.js above the hand, the suggested card or bid ringed, cleared on the events below; a reply whose turnKey's stage, seat or bid count is not the current turn's is dropped); iOS from the build after 1.2.3 (17) (H4)). A tip and the advice of the same decision arrive tip first. Every text is at most 280 characters. Clear it on the next updateTurn, the player's own bidReceived / cardPlayed, hand end, or a turnKey that is not the current turn's. iOS (the build after 1.2.3 (17)) sends the cap and reads it (GameSocketHandler; ServerEvent.assistHint decoded with seq nil, every field optional but kind and headline; TableReducer+Assist: AssistCardView above the hand or the bid panel, the suggested card's glow, the suggested bid's ring, the lightbulb by the hand); builds <= 17 never send the cap, so they keep the private lines. unlimited (additive 2026-11-19, owner "Unlimited, keep notice"): true in a game with a native bot seat (assistState.isFreeHelpGame), where /help has no limit: uses still counts (the room notice "<name> used /help." stays, once per counted turn; the game-end record still marks more than 3 counted uses, profileHandlers.buildGameEndRecord), freeUses stays 3 so shipped decoders keep working, assisted is never true, note never carries the warning or the crossing. Owner wording rule (say nothing): clients show no count and never the words free, unlimited or bot-assisted in such a game (footer just 'What our strongest bot would play', /help described as just 'Ask a bot for advice'); the flag name is internal. Clients also know such a game before any hint or snapshot from their own table state (a seat whose controller is a native bot, snapshot seats[].controller 'bot': web GameState, iOS PlayersSlice; never a lazy or resign bot). The ask's label (the lightbulb, /help in the chat list) is 'Ask a bot for advice' in every game (owner 2026-11-19).

Only when CUT_FOR_A_BUCK is not off, 2 or more members are connected and one of them has the clientHello cap cutForABuck; then the tournament is in phase 'cut' (sockets without the cap see 'round_active'). candidates: the members connected now; the participants are fixed at the gather's end (cutForABuckRound). deckCount: the full deck(s), 54 per 54 players. cutForABuckRound.notes: A round opens: everyone in alive draws one card from the deckCount face-down slots (0..deckCount-1, c2s cutForABuckDraw) within closesInMs (CUT_DRAW_MS, 15 s); then the server draws for whoever has not (cutForABuckDrew auto). A player still in who is disconnected, on a socket without the cap, or away (2 timeouts in a row, until a draw of their own or a return to the lobby) is drawn for at once. reshuffled: fewer cards were left than players, so the full deck(s) were shuffled back (the table cleared). participants is the same list every round.

cutForABuckDrew.notes: A player drew the card in slot (a taken slot went to the nearest free one; a null slot drew a random one). Never the card: every card stays secret until cutForABuckReveal. auto: the server drew for them (disconnected, no cap, away, or the window closed).

cutForABuckLeft.notes: A player still in left the tournament: out (as left). freedSlot: the slot of their unrevealed draw this round, free again. Then, as it falls, cutForABuckWinner (one player left) or cutForABuckReveal (everyone left has drawn).

cutForABuckReveal.notes: Every card of the round, flipped together (draws in participant order). The lowest rank is out (suits never count; 2..A, then LO, then HI): eliminated, everyone tied on it. redraw: every player still in tied, nobody is out. Drawn cards never go back in the deck until a reshuffle. nextInMs: the next cutForABuckRound (CUT_REVEAL_MS, 4 s), or with one player left the time until tournamentComplete (CUT_WINNER_MS, 6 s; cutForABuckWinner follows at once). Members and spectators without the cap get the round as a private system tournamentMessage.

cutForABuckWinner.notes: One player is left: the winner of Cut for a buck ("Just for bragging rights"), with every participant and the rounds drawn. A room system line "<winner> won Cut for a buck." follows; tournamentComplete (with the same cutForABuck) comes CUT_WINNER_MS later.

adminResponse.notes: The reply to adminRequest, to the requesting socket only (requestId and action echoed). failure: forbidden = not an admin right now (the one uniform refusal for every action and target: no account information), invalid = bad args or a wrong typed confirmation, not_found / refused / last_admin / stale_plan (the merge changed since its preview: preview again) / server; counts of what changed), 'tombstone' = only that merged / renamed name was removed (mergedInto names the account it pointed at, which is unchanged). renameAccount: username is the old name, newName the new; every saved session was revoked (the player signs in once with the new name); the old name became a redirect (oldNameKept; mergedInto + renamedAt, so sign-in with the old name and the account's password says "This account is now called X"; nobody else is told the new name); resumed = a second rename with the same names finished a partial one (also when the redirect was never written: oldNameKept then says whether it is now); a player row's renamed = that redirect, renameUnfinished = on a live account, the old name of its rename that stopped partway (the panel's Finish rename sends renameAccount {username: old, newName: the row}); an admin cannot rename their own account (refused). applyMerge / deleteAccount / renameAccount wait in one queue and are authorized again when their turn comes (forbidden if the admin lost the flag or was signed out meanwhile). iOS (from 1.2.2 build 10): AdminSocketHandler hands the reply to AdminApi by requestId (a dictionary read: unknown keys ignored, missing ones defaulted; State/Admin/AdminModels.swift); the reset token is kept in memory only while its sheet is open and never logged. iOS 1.2.0 / 1.2.1 register no handler and never get one (the reply goes only to the requesting socket).

A casual game's voice room (2026-11-16, server/voice/gameVoice.js) adds capable spectators: a newly admitted one gets the players (and, while spectators may talk, the spectators admitted before it), a returning owner (reconnect, /active reclaim) gets the voice spectators too; a block list that is loaded leaves a pair out. Tournament voice (2026-11-24, server/voice/tournamentVoice.js): at a tournament table's seating (right after positionUpdate) each connected human owner gets the owners before it in seat order (sockets with the cap tournamentVoice, or casualSpectators from iOS that starts voice muted: with assist, or build 18 and later; a reconnect there lists the same sockets, never during the seating's reveal hold); in a tournament's voice room (tournament:<id>: members on its lobby screen with the cap tournamentVoice, at most 8) a member entering (tournamentCreated / tournamentJoined) gets the admitted members before it, and a member already in it gets every other one again.

voicePeerLeft.notes: room: a game seat owner dropped (game.broadcast); private: lobby peers (io.to(socketId)) and, since 2026-11-16, a game's voice peers: a voice spectator leaving (to the members, never the room), an entrant dropping or leaving during the draw, a demoted owner socket (watchSeat, both ways), a blocked pair (both ways), the spectator talk switch and its backstop (server/voice/gameVoice.js). Play again (2026-11-16, server/socket/playAgain.js), private, both ways: at a lobby-born game's end between the members moved back to the lobby and every other socket of the game's voice room (main-room spectators, owners not moved) except an older-app owner still on the score screen, whose calls with them linger until it leaves that screen (joinMainRoom, another entry point, a disconnect) or the lobby starts or goes. Every shipped iOS build only drops the peer on a private one.

voiceSettings.notes: New (2026-11-16, family lobbies; private, unsequenced, read by no shipped iOS build). Read by the web (handlers/voiceHandlers.js -> main.js onVoiceSettings) and iOS from 1.2.2 (build 12) (VoiceSocketHandler.applyVoiceSettings). Only to a socket that sent the casualSpectators cap, in a casual game (one started from a lobby; never a tournament table or the ambient demo): at the start (the table's players and the extras), on spectating or admission, as the answer to a setSpectatorsCanTalk from the game, when an owner drops, returns or reclaims a seat, and when an entrant leaves. role: player (a seat owner / entrant in voice), spectator (admitted to the voice room), none (a capable spectator refused: voice is full, 8 people). Since 2026-11-18 (owner: no spectator talk switch) spectatorsCanTalk is always true, canTalk is true for a player and a spectator (false only with role none) and canChange is always false (iOS 12-15 then hide their in-game switch); every field stays for the builds that read them. Until then canTalk could be false for a spectator (the switch off, or a main-room stranger at an all-legacy table), whose listen-only SDP the server gated, and canChange named who could send setSpectatorsCanTalk. host: the lobby host's username.

voiceIceServers.notes: The reply to getVoiceIceServers. iceServers is an RTCPeerConnection iceServers list: turn true = Cloudflare TURN (username / credential on the turn: / turns: entry, valid expiresInSec more seconds; port-53 URLs dropped), false = the public STUN servers both clients used before (expiresInSec null). requestId echoes the request's. Never the API token.

serverShutdown.notes: Every deploy (SIGTERM -> gracefulShutdown): sent to every socket, which is closed about 1 s later (a transport close, so the clients reconnect by themselves). Kept (owner 2026-11-11, V1_REMOVALS #17): web shows a restart banner and, after reconnect, what ended (the game, the watched game, the lobby or the tournament the player was in; nothing for the main room); the message text is not read. iOS 1.1.0 ignores it (no handler); iOS 1.2 shows a "Restarting for an update" toast and, after the restore, one alert for what ended (RestartNotice.swift; the message text is not read).

serverError.notes: Every app-level server error (V1_REMOVALS #1): the wrappers' rate limit / Joi validation / unexpected exception, a handler's refusal, a chat command error. Phase A (2026-11-11) added it as the twin of the v1 `error`; phase B (2026-11-12, once iOS 1.1.0 was gated) dropped `error`, so this is the only copy. code: rateLimit / validation / server, or rejected (a handler's {message} refusal); handler: the c2s event it answers (the registered socket.on name: errorHandler options.event, else the schema; or the handler that refused; the chat events: mainRoomChat / lobbyChat / tournamentChat, in-game chat chatMessage), null when unknown. Read by web (main.js onServerFailure: a toast, and a table resync for playCard / playerBid / requestSnapshot; adminApi.js fails a dropped admin request fast as rate_limited on {code:'rateLimit', handler:'adminRequest'}) and iOS 1.2.0 (SocketService handleServerError: toast + routeTableError); its own name because Socket.IO-Client-Swift reserves 'error' for transport errors (clientEvent .error, which 1.2.0 still listens to for those). Gated builds 1 and 2 never get it (upgradeGate.js registers no handler for them).
